function.name: generate_image_tool
function.description: Generates an image based on the provided description and saves it with the specified file name. The image description should be detailed to ensure the resulting image matches the desired subject and surroundings; otherwise, these aspects will be chosen randomly. This function is not intended for generating images from textual data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

function.name: tts_tool
function.description: Converts the provided text content to speech and saves the resulting audio to a file. This function is intended for voice narration and should be used accordingly. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The text content that needs to be converted to speech.

function.name: write_markdown_tool

This function should be used when there is a need to persist text data in Markdown format as a result of a user action or a process that requires saving information in a structured text file. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The Markdown formatted text content to be written to the file.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the Markdown content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: write_html_tool
function.description: Writes an HTML file to disk with the given content. Ensures HTML tags within the content are properly closed. This function should be used when there is a need to save HTML content to a file as part of a 'save' operation. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: search_web_tool
function.description: Executes a search query using the DuckDuckGo search engine and returns a specified number of search results from a given source. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, with a default value that allows for a reasonable amount of time for most web pages to load.

user_agent.description: The User-Agent string to be used for the HTTP request to simulate a particular browser, which is optional. Some websites may require this for access.

Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to launch a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that: | Requirement | How it’s satisfied | |-------------|--------------------| | **GPU** – NVIDIA RTX A6000 | `nvidia-tesla-a6000` accelerator | | **OS** – Ubuntu 20.04 LTS | `ubuntu-os-cloud/ubuntu-2004-focal-v20230912` image | | **Machine type** – 8 vCPU / 32 GB RAM (adjustable) | `e2-standard-8` | | **Zone** – `us-central1-a` (change as needed) | `us-central1-a` | | **Project** – your GCP project ID | `YOUR_PROJECT_ID` | --- ## 1. gcloud CLI command ```bash # 1️⃣ Set variables PROJECT="YOUR_PROJECT_ID" ZONE="us-central1-a" INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu" MACHINE_TYPE="e2-standard-8" # 8 vCPU, 32 GB RAM IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts" IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud" # 2️⃣ Create the instance gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \ --project="$PROJECT" \ --zone="$ZONE" \ --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \ --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \ --image-family="$IMAGE_FAMILY" \ --image-project="$IMAGE_PROJECT" \ --boot-disk-size=100GB \ --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \ --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \ --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \ --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh # optional: add a startup script ``` > **Notes** > * Replace `YOUR_PROJECT_ID` with your actual GCP project ID. > * The `--accelerator` flag attaches one RTX A6000 GPU. > * The `--boot-disk-size` and `--boot-disk-type` flags give you a 100 GB SSD boot disk; adjust if you need more space. > * The `--scopes` flag gives the instance full Cloud Platform access; you can restrict it if you prefer. --- ## 2. REST API (JSON body) If you prefer to use the REST API directly (e.g., from a custom script or Terraform), here’s the exact JSON payload you would POST to: ```json { "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu", "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/e2-standard-8", "disks": [ { "boot": true, "initializeParams": { "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts", "diskSizeGb": 100, "diskType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-ssd" } } ], "networkInterfaces": [ { "network": "global/networks/default", "accessConfigs": [ { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" } ] } ], "serviceAccounts": [ { "email": "default", "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"] } ], "accelerators": [ { "acceleratorCount": 1, "acceleratorType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000" } ], "metadata": { "items": [ { "key": "startup-script", "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535" } ] } } ``` ### How to POST this JSON ```bash curl -X POST \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d @instance.json \ "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/instances" ``` > Replace `YOUR_PROJECT_ID` with your project ID and `instance.json` with the path to the JSON file above. --- ## 3. Quick checklist | Step | Command / Action | Why | |------|------------------|-----| | Enable Compute Engine API | `gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com` | Required for API calls | | Create service account & key (if using REST) | `gcloud iam service-accounts create my-sa --display-name="My SA"`
`gcloud iam service-accounts keys create key.json --iam-account=my-sa@YOUR_PROJECT_ID.iam.gserviceaccount.com` | For authentication | | Grant GPU quota | `gcloud compute accelerator-types describe nvidia-tesla-a6000 --zone us-central1-a` | Verify you have GPU quota | | Launch instance | `gcloud compute instances create ...` or REST POST | Creates the VM | --- ### Final tip If you’re using Terraform, the same configuration can be expressed in HCL: ```hcl resource "google_compute_instance" "rtx_a6000" { name = "rtx-a6000-ubuntu" machine_type = "e2-standard-8" zone = "us-central1-a" boot_disk { initialize_params { image = "ubuntu-os-cloud/ubuntu-2004-lts" size = 100 type = "pd-ssd" } } network_interface { network = "default" access_config {} } service_account { scopes = ["cloud-platform"] } guest_accelerator { type = "nvidia-tesla-a6000" count = 1 } metadata_startup_script = <<-EOT #!/bin/bash apt-get update apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535 EOT } ``` Happy GPU computing! 🚀
